content.what_it_is: Python plotting script that loads a Tohoku depth grid from a hard-coded workstation path (L10), derives half-degree coordinate arrays from its shape (L13-L18), plots negated depth with a terrain colormap (L25-L32), adds a labeled colorbar, and saves tsunami_bathy.png (L35-L39).
entities: numpy module alias np imported at L4
matplotlib.pyplot alias plt imported at L5
depth array dep defined at L10
array dimensions n and m defined at L13
grid spacings dx and dy defined at L14-L15
coordinate arrays x and y defined at L17-L18
figure dimensions wid and length defined at L21-L22

equations.expr: x = np.asarray([float(xa)*dx+132.01667 for xa in range(m)])
equations.ref: longitude coordinate array from column indices

equations.expr: y = np.asarray([float(ya)*dy-59.98333 for ya in range(n)])
equations.ref: latitude coordinate array from row indices
plot negated depth with terrain colormap

calls: np.asarray, float, and range at L17-L18
unresolved: Portability/interface defect at L8-L10: the comment asks the user to provide a folder path, but no fdir input exists and np.loadtxt uses one developer-specific absolute path, so the script fails on other machines unless source code is edited.

Matplotlib pcolor at L29 uses center-length x/y vectors with an equally shaped dep array; depending on the installed Matplotlib shading default/version this can either discard a boundary row/column or reject same-sized coordinates, and no shading mode is specified.
